results.title: Pricing under uncertainty: Forward and option pricing in sports markets - ScienceDirect
results.content: # Pricing under uncertainty: Forward and option pricing in sports markets. Currently, tournament game tickets are sold in advance, before the teams playing in the final games are known (we refer to this strategy as “advance” pricing). We believe our work is the first to study the concept of forward pricing in consumer markets. While Sainam, Balasubramanian, and Bayus (2010) study option ticket pricing, we go beyond their work and compare how forward pricing performs relative to option pricing and conventional advance pricing. At an average price of $2,500 for the 2022 Superbowl, the 70,000-seat SoFi stadium generated about $66.5 million in ticket sales.3 Consumers (also referred to as fans henceforth) avoid purchasing advance tickets in the face of uncertainty; instead, they often purchase from ticket brokers such as StubHub, SeatGeek, and Ticketmaster (“third-party” henceforth) after uncertainty related to the playing teams is resolved. For example, Sainam, Balasubramanian, and Bayus (2015) empirically examine the purchase and resale of ticket forwards in a third-party marketplace—a different angle from the research questions studied in this paper. The forward ticket concept also been implemented in the College Football National Championship Game as “RSVPs” (Arnold, 2019): “RSVPs are team and game-specific reservations that allow college football fans guaranteed access to purchase tickets at face-value, provided their team is playing. In 3 The market: Definition of fan types, 4 Theory: Analytical models of forward pricing, we model forward and option pricing with and without capacity constraints. We model forward pricing in a market with team- and game-based fans. Our primary focus is to provide the first formal model of forward pricing in the marketing literature, and to compare such pricing with other mechanisms. Correspondingly, the modest goals of the empirical analysis of ticket forwards are to serve as a touchstone for the assumptions in the theoretical model, examine fan comfort with the forward pricing concept, and provide some preliminary, exploratory insights into the performance of the different pricing mechanisms. Forward pricing is well-suited to elimination-style tournaments where there is a) uncertainty regarding the team that will ultimately make it at each stage and b) different consumer preferences for the playing teams—represented as team- and game-based fans.

results.content: # Mastering Seasonal Considerations for SaaS Pricing Tests. Yet many executives overlook a critical factor that influences pricing effectiveness: seasonality. Understanding how market trends fluctuate throughout the year is fundamental to executing successful pricing tests and optimizing revenue. ## Why Seasonal Factors Matter in SaaS Pricing. Unlike traditional retail where seasonal pricing strategies are obvious (holiday discounts, back-to-school promotions), seasonality in SaaS operates more subtly but with equal impact. According to McKinsey's SaaS Pricing Benchmark study, companies that adjust their testing schedules to account for seasonal variations see 12-18% higher conversion rates on pricing changes compared to those implementing year-round uniform strategies.
